rows.jp: 「実はな、俺は記憶ソーシツだ」

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "Truth is, I got some memories missing."

rows.jp: 唐突に、ヤツは言った。
rows.en: He announced it out of nowhere.

ghs.en: Out of the blue the guy said that.

rows.jp: 「主人公みたいだな」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Like a main character innit."
Shinkawa: "?"

rows.jp: 「なんでもない。忘れてくれ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Nothing, nothing. Just forget it."

rows.jp: 新川は語った。

ghs.en: Shinkawa spoke.

rows.jp: 少年期の記憶がないこと。
rows.en: He remembered nothing of his childhood.

ghs.en: He has no memories of the time he was a boy,

rows.jp: 先端恐怖症であること。
rows.en: He had a phobia of sharp points.

ghs.en: he has a phobia of things with pointed ends,

rows.jp: 森の暗がりに病的な恐怖を感じること。
rows.en: Dark places in the woods filled him with pathological terror.

ghs.en:
and the darkness of the woods makes him feel
a morbid fear.

rows.jp: なにかがあったのだ。昔。

ghs.en: Something had happened. A long time ago.

rows.jp: けど内容は知らないのだという。
rows.en: But he had no idea what.

ghs.en: But what, exactly, he doesn't know.

rows.jp: 霧の両親も教えてはくれなかったらしい。
rows.en: Apparently Kiri’s parents had never told him either.

ghs.en: Kiri's parents didn't seem to want to tell him.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says Kiri's parents apparently did not tell him. The English changes the completed refusal or omission into an inferred lack of desire.

highlights.text: didn't seem to want to tell him

rows.jp: そして新川豊に家族がいないこと。
rows.en: And Yutaka Shinkawa had no family.

ghs.en:
And then, Shinkawa Yutaka spoke of how he is
without family.
ghs.assessment: This is another fact in the narrator's list: Yutaka has no family. The English invents a speech act by Shinkawa and shifts the past account into present tense.

highlights.text:
Shinkawa Yutaka spoke of how he is
without family

rows.jp: 全ては闇の中。

ghs.en: All is in darkness.

rows.jp: そしてついには、霧とともに群青送り。
rows.en: Until at last he and Kiri were both shipped off to Gunjo.

ghs.en:
And then, in the end, he was sent to Gunjou
together with Kiri.

rows.jp: 「……むぐむぐ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "...munch, munch."

rows.jp: 俺はピザを貪り食いながら聞いた。
rows.en: I listened while devouring a pizza.

ghs.en: I listened to all that while greedily devouring a pizza.

rows.jp: デリバリーしたピザだった。

ghs.en: It was a delivery pizza.

rows.jp: 当時、俺は非常に裕福であり、昼食は出前を取っていた。
rows.en: I was extremely wealthy in those days, so I had lunch brought in.

ghs.en: Those days I was uncommonly affluent, therefore I had lunch delivered.

rows.jp: 基本的に心の治療という名目もあってか、群青での校則はあってなきに等しい。
rows.en: Maybe because the whole place ostensibly existed to treat our minds, Gunjo’s school rules might as well not have existed.

ghs.en: Basically, with the pretext of healing the heart, Gunjou's school regulations are next to ignorable.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says the school rules at Gunjou are virtually nonexistent, partly under the pretext of mental treatment. The English says existing rules are merely ignorable and calques mental care as healing the heart. Gunjou itself is an acceptable ASCII long-vowel spelling and is not part of the error.
ghs.remedy: Say that, partly under the pretext of mental treatment, the school's rules are virtually nonexistent.

highlights.text: school regulations are next to ignorable

rows.jp: ピザを取るのを止めたら、情緒不安定になるかも知れないからだ。
rows.en: If they stopped me from ordering pizza, I might become emotionally unstable.

ghs.en: If I was prevented from having my pizza, I might just become emotionally unstable.

rows.jp: 治療という名目で人を隔離しているこの学校は、自意識さえあれば無法地帯だった。
rows.en: At this school, which isolated people in the name of treatment, anyone with a sense of self could get away with anything.

ghs.en: The mere possession of self-awareness made a lawless space of this school designed to isolate people with the pretext of medical treatment.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says the school was a lawless zone for anyone still possessing a sense of self. The English makes possession of self-awareness the cause that transformed the school.

highlights.text: The mere possession of self-awareness made a lawless space of this school

rows.jp: ……孤島の牢獄めいて。

ghs.en: ...it's like an island prison.

rows.jp: 「うーむ、そうだったか。記憶ソーシツ。うーむ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Hmmm, that's how it is. Memories missing. Hmmm."

rows.jp: 俺は熟考した。そして、
rows.en: I considered the matter deeply. Then—

ghs.en: I gave it deep consideration. And then,

rows.jp: 「ＯＫ！」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Okieh!"

rows.jp: 「そうか……まあそういうと思ったがな……」
rows.en: “Right... More or less what I expected you to say...”

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "Right... well I thought, you know..."
ghs.assessment: Shinkawa says he figured Taichi would say that. The English omits the predicted speech and turns it into a vague act of thinking.

rows.jp: 「俺は記憶ソーシツの新川を肯定するぞ。けど記憶喪失でない新川はご免被る」
rows.en: “I approve of Am-NEE-siac Shinkawa. But Shinkawa with his memory intact? No, thank you.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I'll be positive on Shinkawa who has memories missing. But Shinkawa without memory loss is too unpleasant to accept."
ghs.assessment: Taichi says he accepts the amnesiac Shinkawa but wants no part of a version without amnesia. The English uses the nonidiomatic 'positive on' and invents unpleasantness as the reason for refusal.

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "......"

rows.jp: そんな気怠い空間に、霧が来た。
rows.en: Kiri entered that languid little space.

ghs.en: And in that listless space came Kiri.

rows.jp: 「また二人でつるんでる」

ghs.en: Kiri: "You two mate-ing again."
ghs.assessment: つるむ means the two are hanging out together again. 'Mate-ing' is a malformed coinage that suggests sex or animal breeding.

rows.jp: 「霧ちんだ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Oh, Kiri-chin."

rows.jp: 「……霧ちんって呼ばないでください」

ghs.en: Kiri: "...please do not call me 'Kiri-chin'."

rows.jp: 「だって霧ちんじゃん」

ghs.en: Taichi: "But you're Kiri-chin ain'tcha."

rows.jp: 「霧です」

ghs.en: Kiri: "Just Kiri."

rows.jp: 「じゃ霧」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Kiri then."

rows.jp: 「呼び捨てにしないでください！」

ghs.en: Kiri: "Please do not call me without honorific!"

rows.jp: 「どうしろと」
rows.en: “Then what am I supposed to call you?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Make up your mind!"
ghs.assessment: Taichi asks what form of address she wants him to use. The English instead accuses her of indecision and orders her to resolve it.

rows.jp: 「なあ豊？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Right, Yutaka?"

rows.jp: 寝ていた。

ghs.en: He fell asleep.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says they discover him already asleep. The English depicts the event of falling asleep at that moment.

rows.jp: 「すぐ寝るな、コイツ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Quick to sleep this guy."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese remarks that he falls asleep quickly. The English uses an adjective phrase before an unintegrated subject noun phrase.

rows.jp: 「……昔からそうなんです」

ghs.en: Kiri: "...he has been like this since a long time ago."
ghs.assessment: English uses 'for' with a duration: 'for a long time.'

rows.jp: 「後遺症みたいなものらしくて……」

ghs.en: Kiri: "They seem to be something like after effects..."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese calls the sleepiness something like a singular aftereffect. The English uses a plural pronoun without an antecedent and splits the compound 'aftereffects.'

highlights.text: They seem to be something like after effects

rows.jp: 「ああ、例の記憶喪失ってやつ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ahhh, like how he has memory loss, then."

rows.jp: 「……豊に聞いたんですか」

ghs.en: Kiri: "...did Yutaka tell you?"

rows.jp: 「今さっき」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Just now."

rows.jp: 「そうですか……信頼されてるんですね」

ghs.en: Kiri: "So he did... that means you are trusted then."

rows.jp: 「って？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Wha-?"

rows.jp: 「前の学校で、友達なんていませんでしたから。兄にも私にも」
rows.en: “Neither my brother nor I had any friends at our old school.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Because, at our previous school we did not have friends. Neither I nor Ani."
ghs.assessment: 兄 means her older brother. The English leaves it as an unexplained Japanese kinship term instead of translating it.

rows.jp: よくあることだった。

ghs.en: That happened frequently,

rows.jp: 特に適応試験の結果は、よく漏れた。
rows.en: The results of the adaptation tests were especially prone to leaking.

ghs.en: especially since the results of the Conformity Test were frequently leaked.

rows.jp: 「友達だった人にも、裏切られて……誰も信用できなくなって……」
rows.en: “Even the people we thought were friends betrayed us... until we couldn’t trust anyone...”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Even the people who were friends betrayed us... we could no longer trust anyone..."

rows.jp: 「誰も傷つけてないのに、みんなから傷つけられて」
rows.en: “We never hurt anyone, but everyone hurt us.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "We did not hurt anyone, but still everybody hurt us."

rows.jp: 「そして牙を剥くこともある」

ghs.en: Taichi: "And then you went and bared your fangs."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese generalizes that victims may sometimes bare their fangs in response. The English assigns the action specifically to Kiri, shifts it into completed past, and adds reproachful 'went and.'

highlights.text: you went and bared your fangs

rows.jp: 「攻撃されたら、身を守るのが当然じゃないですか」
rows.en: “If someone attacks you, of course you defend yourself.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "If you are attacked, is it not natural you would protect yourself?"

rows.jp: 「そういう考え方もある」
rows.en: “That is one way of looking at it.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "That is one way of thinking, yes."

rows.jp: 「けど身を守った猛獣は、撃ち殺されるのが世の常なんだよ」
rows.en: “But the way of the world is to shoot the beast that bares its fangs in self-defense.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But in this world, it's ordinary for wild beasts that defend themselves to be shot to death."

rows.jp: 「……人間じゃないですか」

ghs.en: Kiri: "...are you not human?"
ghs.assessment: Kiri protests that the supposedly wild beasts are human beings. The English instead asks whether Taichi himself is human.

rows.jp: 低く、霧は吐いた。
rows.en: Kiri spat the words under her breath.

ghs.en: So spat out Kiri, tone lowering.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says Kiri spits the words out in a low voice. The English uses an archaic inversion and makes her tone an ungoverned progressive fragment.

highlights.text: So spat out Kiri, tone lowering.

rows.jp: 義憤。

ghs.en: Righteous indignation.

rows.jp: 現代を生きるには、霧はまっすぐにすぎた。
rows.en: Kiri was too straight and true for the modern world.

ghs.en: Kiri was far too straightforward to live in modern times.

rows.jp: 「中にはね……本当に人じゃないのもいるんだ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Inside here... truly, there's something not of the person."
ghs.assessment: Taichi says some among them truly are no longer human. The English substitutes a place called 'inside here,' changes people to one thing, and produces the non-English phrase 'not of the person.'

highlights.text: Inside here... truly, there's something not of the person.

rows.jp: 「たまにさ、周囲の人間のこと、どうでもいいって思っちゃうことってない？」
rows.en: “Don’t you ever find yourself thinking that you couldn’t care less about the people around you?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Every once in a while, when you think about the people around you, don't you find yourself thinking they are sort of, like, irrelevant?"

rows.jp: 「俺はたまにある。たまにね。けど……完全にそうなったらおしまいだ」
rows.en: “I do sometimes. Only sometimes. But... if that ever becomes absolute, it’s over.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I do, at times. At times, mind you. But... if I became completely like that, I'd be done for."

rows.jp: 「頑張って生きないとな。少しでも奴らに尻尾を振って、あの普通の人とかいう連中に、媚びをうってでもさ……生きんと」
rows.en: “We have to work at staying alive. Wag our tails for them, grovel before those so-called normal people if we must... Anything to live.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I just do my best to live. I wag my tail a bit to those people that call themselves normal, launch myself into flattery a bit to them... I gotta live."
ghs.assessment: Taichi says he must work to survive even if that means wagging his tail and currying favor with so-called normal people. The English turns necessity into a current habit and says he 'launches' himself into flattery.

highlights.text: Taichi: "I just do my best to live. I wag my tail a bit to those people that call themselves normal, launch myself into flattery a bit to them... I gotta live."

rows.jp: 「それで変な行動を？」
rows.en: “Is that why you act so strangely?”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Is that why you act so weird?"

rows.jp: 「さあ……考えたこともないや」
rows.en: “Who knows? I’ve never thought about it.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Dunno... never really gave it much thought."

rows.jp: 「……君もそうなんだぞ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "...you're also like that."

rows.jp: 「え……わたしも、ですか？」

ghs.en: Kiri: "Eh... me... as well?"

rows.jp: 「生存したかろうが」

ghs.en: Taichi: "You wanna live, don't you."

rows.jp: 「わたしは……」

ghs.en: Kiri: "I..."

rows.jp: 「わたしは」

ghs.en: Kiri: "I...!"

rows.jp: 顔を伏せる。自分を抱く。
rows.en: She lowered her face and folded her arms around herself.

ghs.en: She lowers her face. And hugs herself.

rows.jp: 「世界が恐くてたまらない、です」

ghs.en: Kiri: "The world is unbearably frightening, yes."

rows.jp: 「どんなところが？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "What part of it?"

rows.jp: 「……悪意が」

ghs.en: Kiri: "...the malice."

rows.jp: 「みんなの悪意が……」

ghs.en: Kiri: "Everybody's malicious..."
ghs.assessment: Kiri identifies everyone's malice as what frightens her. The English instead directly characterizes every person as malicious.

rows.jp: 「誰も……優しくない……優しさが少ない……」
rows.en: “Nobody is... kind. There’s so little kindness...”

ghs.en: Kiri: "No one... no kindness... not a shred of kindness..."

rows.jp: 震える。

ghs.en: She's shaking.

rows.jp: そう。

ghs.en: Yes.

rows.jp: 彼女もまた、望んでここに来たわけでない。
rows.en: She had not come here by choice either.

ghs.en: She, herself, is not here because she has wished it.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says she did not come there by choice. The English mixes present location with present perfect wishing in a nonidiomatic causal construction.

highlights.text: is not here because she has wished it

rows.jp: ここに来るしかなかった。
rows.en: This was the only place left for her.

ghs.en: She was given no choice but to come here.

rows.jp: 国はそう定め給うた。

ghs.en: The country has so decreed,

rows.jp: 逆らうことは許されない。

ghs.en: and opposition is not tolerated.

rows.jp: 「……人間なんて、なくなる時にはあっさりなくなるって思ってます……だって、世界にはほとんど何もないから……」
rows.en: “...I think human beings could just disappear. Just like that... Because there’s almost nothing in the world...”

ghs.en: Kiri: "...I think that humans, when they depart, will just vanish like that... because in this world there is nearly nothing."
ghs.assessment: Kiri says humanity or human beings can disappear with shocking ease when the time comes. 'Depart' reframes this as individual death or leave-taking and the future tense makes it a prediction.

highlights.text: humans, when they depart, will just vanish like that

rows.jp: 「きっと『何もない』方が多いんです。『なにかある』方は、ちょっとだけなんです！」
rows.en: “There must be far more ‘nothing’ than ‘something.’ ‘Something’ is only this tiny little bit!”

ghs.en: Kiri: "I am sure, there is Nothing in so much. In just so little is there Anything!"
ghs.assessment: Kiri says the realm of nothingness is surely much larger and the realm where something exists only a little. The English uses two ungrammatical inversions and fails to make the comparative relation intelligible.

highlights.text: there is Nothing in so much. In just so little is there Anything!

rows.jp: 「いつ押し流されてしまうかもわからないって……思って」
rows.en: “And I keep thinking... it could all be swept away at any moment...”

ghs.en: Kiri: "And we won't know when we will be washed away... I think."

rows.jp: 「その……ＳＦみたいな、人類滅亡とか？」
rows.en: “You mean... some sci-fi scenario where humanity goes extinct?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Sort of... an SF-like thing, the Fall of Mankind?"

rows.jp: 「そういうのとは違って……そういう理由があるのとは違って……」
rows.en: “Not like that... Not something with a reason behind it...”

ghs.en: Kiri: "It is different from that... it is different in how there is a reason in that..."
ghs.assessment: Kiri says this differs from scenarios where there is an identifiable cause. The English stacks two locative 'in' phrases and does not state the contrast clearly.

highlights.text: it is different in how there is a reason in that

rows.jp: 「夢から覚めたみたいに」

ghs.en: Kiri: "This will be like waking up from a dream."
ghs.assessment: Kiri makes an atemporal comparison to waking from a dream. The English invents a future event and an explicit subject.

rows.jp: 「いがみあってばかりで、こわいだけなのに……」
rows.en: “All we ever do is fight, and it’s so frightening...”

ghs.en: Kiri: "If all is quarreling, then everything is scary..."
ghs.assessment: Kiri says people do nothing but quarrel and that this is merely frightening. The English changes the statement into an ungrammatical conditional.

highlights.text: If all is quarreling, then everything is scary

rows.jp: 「けどある日、突然すべてがなくなって……ちっぽけな世界で……もし自分ひとりが取り残されたらって考えると……」
rows.en: “But then one day, everything suddenly disappears... and if I were left all alone in that tiny little world...”

ghs.en: Kiri: "But one day, all of a sudden everything will be no more... and I keep thinking, what if I was the only one that will be left behind... in that tiny worthless world..."

rows.jp: 「わたし……わたしは……」

ghs.en: Kiri: "I... I'd..."

rows.jp: 「佐倉霧」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Sakura Kiri."

rows.jp: 呼び戻す。

ghs.en: I call her back.

rows.jp: 沈みかけていた表情にさっと色がさす。
rows.en: Color rushed back into her fading face.

ghs.en: Color sprung quickly in that face that had sunk into depression.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese metaphor says color returns to her expression as it is sinking. The English diagnoses the face as having sunk into depression and uses past perfect.

highlights.text: face that had sunk into depression

rows.jp: 「あ……すいません……」

ghs.en: Kiri: "Ah... apologies..."

rows.jp: 「悪意も恐い、一人も恐い……か」
rows.en: “So you’re afraid of malice, and afraid of being alone.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Afraid of people's malice, and afraid of being alone as well... then."

rows.jp: 「座ったら、ピザも食ってよし」
rows.en: “Sit down. Then you may have pizza.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Sit down, have some pizza too."

rows.jp: 「食いブチ、一人寝たし」
rows.en: “One mouth less to feed, since somebody fell asleep.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "One of the food expenses here's asleep."
Shinkawa: "......"
Kiri: "...huh."

rows.jp: ゆるゆる座る。ピザには手をつけない。
rows.en: She lowered herself slowly into a seat but did not touch the pizza.

ghs.en: She slowly sits down. She does not lay hand on the pizza.
ghs.assessment: The English singular count noun requires a determiner or possessive: 'lay a hand on.'

rows.jp: 感情の揺り戻し。

ghs.en: It's emotional swingback.

rows.jp: 少しぼんやりしていた。
rows.en: She still looked a little dazed.

ghs.en: She was just a bit out of it.

rows.jp: 「挙げ句の果てに流刑地に送られたっと」
rows.en: “And after all that, off you went to a penal colony.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "And to top it all of, you were sent to the penal colony."
ghs.assessment: The fixed phrase is 'to top it all off.'

rows.jp: 「……流刑地なんですか、ここ」

ghs.en: Kiri: "...so is this a penal colony, then?"

rows.jp: 「そうだよ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Indeed it is."

rows.jp: 「けど悪意はない。いじめも。見てみろよ」
rows.en: “But there’s no malice here. No bullying. Look.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But there's no malice. Bullying neither. Look around!"
ghs.assessment: The Japanese adds that there is no bullying either. The English uses an isolated noun with a negative additive adverb but no predicate.

rows.jp: 周囲を示す。

ghs.en: I point around us.

rows.jp: 昼時。

ghs.en: Noon. Lunchtime.

rows.jp: 自力で食事を取れる者が、ぽつぽつと食事をしている。
rows.en: Here and there, the students capable of getting their own food were eating lunch.

ghs.en: Those who could eat by their own strength were eating, bit by bit.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says people able to feed themselves eat here and there around the room. The English literalizes independent ability as physical strength and makes ぽつぽつ modify the incremental manner of eating.

highlights.text: by their own strength were eating, bit by bit

rows.jp: 集まりはなく、全員一人で食べている。
rows.en: No groups. Every one of them ate alone.

ghs.en: There are no gatherings, and every person is eating by themselves.

rows.jp: 会話もない。

ghs.en: Conversations neither.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese adds that there is no conversation either. The English lacks a predicate.

rows.jp: 俺と新川が話していたくらいだ。
rows.en: Shinkawa and I had been the sole exception.

ghs.en: The chat between me and Shinkawa had been about the only one.

rows.jp: 「みんな穏やかに過ごしている」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Everyone's passing time in tranquility."

rows.jp: 「ある意味、一人で生きる強さを持った連中だ」
rows.en: “In one sense, these people possess the strength to live alone.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "In a sense, they have the strength to live alone."

rows.jp: 「人と繋がる必要もなく、一人で完結している」
rows.en: “They need no connection to anyone else. Each is complete in isolation.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "With no necessity to form connection with people, they become complete on their own."

rows.jp: 「完成された人類だ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Mankind perfected."

rows.jp: 「そんなの……おかしいです」

ghs.en: Kiri: "But that is... weird."

rows.jp: 「未熟なのに人と繋がると、齟齬(そご)は起きる」
rows.en: “When people connect before they’re mature enough, they clash.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "When people become connected despite being inexperienced, discordances occur."
ghs.assessment: 齟齬 means frictions, mismatches, or misunderstandings. The rare plural 'discordances' is a technical calque rather than natural English for interpersonal conflict.

rows.jp: 「それもえてして、普通の人々の間で起こるじゃないか」
rows.en: “And doesn’t that happen most often among ordinary people?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "And those frequently occur between normal people as well, don't they."

rows.jp: 「だから人は、完璧になったら一人で事足りるべきだ」
rows.en: “So once a person is complete, they ought to need no one else.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Therefore, if people become perfect, they ought be satisfied with solitude."
ghs.assessment: Standard English requires the infinitive marker: 'ought to be.'

ghs.en: Kiri: "..."

rows.jp: 「食わないの？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Not eating?"

rows.jp: 「あ……人の手をつけたもの食べるの、無理なんです……」
rows.en: “Oh... I can’t eat things other people have touched...”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Ah... eating things that other people have touched, I just cannot..."

rows.jp: 「潔癖性なんだ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Mysophobia, isn't it."

rows.jp: 「……男の人のは、特に……」

ghs.en: Kiri: "...by males, especially..."

rows.jp: 「男性恐怖症でもあるのか」

ghs.en: Taichi: "You've also androphobia?"
ghs.assessment: The English question is missing the verb 'got' or 'have.'

rows.jp: 「あ、こっちのは、別に……ただなんとなくで……男の人って……不潔だから」
rows.en: “No, that part isn’t... There’s no particular reason... Men are just... dirty.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Ah, not that, not really... it's just that somehow... males are... unclean, that's all."

rows.jp: 「むちゃくちゃ言うな、おまえ」
rows.en: “That’s a hell of a thing to say.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Don't you be talking crazy now."

rows.jp: 思春期の女の子が抱きがちな、単なる異性への意識か。
rows.en: Or maybe it was just the ordinary awareness of the opposite sex that came with being a teenage girl.

ghs.en: It's something a girl in puberty is liable to have, perhaps, merely an awareness of the opposite gender.

rows.jp: 容易に敵意になるし、平時においては萎縮を招く。
rows.en: It could easily turn into hostility; in ordinary situations, it made her shrink into herself.

ghs.en: It easily becomes hostility, and generates withering in times of peace.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says this awareness makes her shrink back or become timid in ordinary situations. The English turns that emotional inhibition into plant-like withering and misreads 平時 as peacetime.

highlights.text: generates withering in times of peace

ghs.en: Kiri: "......" (fidget, fidget)

rows.jp: ……今のように。

ghs.en: ...like now.

rows.jp: ということは、裏を返せばＨなことに興味しんしんってことだ。
rows.en: Which, viewed from the other side, meant she was intensely curious about sex.

ghs.en: Or rather, to view it in another way, this is an overflowing curiosity about things sexual.

rows.jp: わーい。

ghs.en: Weeee.

rows.jp: 「いや、喜んでどうする……」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ahhh, I'm happy and I shouldn't be..."
ghs.assessment: 喜んでどうする is Taichi rebuking himself: 'Why am I celebrating?' The English states a condition of happiness and a separate normative prohibition.

highlights.text: I'm happy and I shouldn't be

rows.jp: 豊の未来妻を奪うわけにはいかない。
rows.en: I could hardly steal Yutaka’s future bride.

ghs.en: It would be improper to forcibly steal Yutaka's future wife.

rows.jp: 「あの、さっきの話ですけど……」

ghs.en: Kiri: "Uhm, but, about what we were talking about before..."

rows.jp: 「悪意はないのかも知れないですけど……この学校は……なんだか『何もない』部分が広い気がして……話しかけても、誰も答えてくれないし」
rows.en: “There may not be any malice... but at this school... the parts where there’s ‘nothing’ feel so enormous... I speak to people, and nobody answers...”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Maybe there is no malice, but... somehow I feel that the parts with Nothing here are vast... even if you get close and talk to someone, they don't reply."

rows.jp: 「そりゃ別に無視してるわけじゃない。法則が違うんだよ」
rows.en: “They aren’t ignoring you. They just obey different rules.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well now, it's not like they're really ignoring you. The laws are just different."

rows.jp: 「……ほうそく？」

ghs.en: Kiri: "...laws?"

rows.jp: 疑問まじりに反復する様子が、年相応に幼く見える。
rows.en: The questioning way she repeated the word made her look as young as she was.

ghs.en: A repetition mixed with a question gives her a look of youth appropriate to her age.

rows.jp: こっちが本当の霧だと悟った。
rows.en: And I realized that this was the real Kiri.

ghs.en: This, I realized, was the real Kiri:

rows.jp: この人見知りをする、口べたでおどおどした少女が。
rows.en: This shy, inarticulate, easily frightened girl.

ghs.en: this hesitant young tongue-tied girl that is shy around strangers.

rows.jp: 「チャンネルが違うというか……交差しないというか……」
rows.en: “It’s like we’re on different channels... like our signals never cross...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I could say the Channel is different... or should I say there is no way to make yourselves Cross..."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese tentatively says that their channels do not intersect. The English introduces a second-person reflexive object, turns the relation into inability, and uses 'Cross' as an ungrammatical infinitive.

highlights.text: there is no way to make yourselves Cross

rows.jp: うまく説明できない。
rows.en: I could not put it into words very well.

ghs.en: I can't really explain it well.

rows.jp: 「霧ちんも俺も、ベースの精神状態はノーマルだからさ。ノーマルじゃないベースのやつとは規格が違うわけだ」
rows.en: “You and I start from a normal state of mind, Kiri-kins. Anyone who doesn’t is built to different specifications.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "'Cause you and me, Kiri-chin, our base mental condition is normal. Those whose base is not normal got different standards."

rows.jp: 「相手の法則にのっとって接触すれば、会話は成立するさ」
rows.en: “Meet them on their terms, and you can have a conversation.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "If you contact the other party while conforming to their rules, you can construct conversations."
ghs.assessment: 会話は成立する means communication or conversation can take place. English speakers do not normally 'construct conversations' in this sense.

rows.jp: 「……どうやって……そんな法則を……」
rows.en: “...But how do you... learn those rules...?”

ghs.en: Kiri: "...how do you learn... these rules..."

rows.jp: 「観察力があれば。そうだな……たとえば」
rows.en: “If you’re observant. Let’s see... for example.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Powers of observation are needed. Right, then... for example."

rows.jp: 手近な席に座っている暗そうな眼鏡の女子のもとに。
rows.en: I approached a gloomy-looking girl in glasses at a nearby seat.

ghs.en: Sitting in a seat at hand was a girl with glasses and mood dark. I approach her.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese describes a gloomy-looking girl with glasses. 'With ... mood dark' is not an English attributive construction.

highlights.text: a girl with glasses and mood dark

rows.jp: 実は彼女と俺は、交易をしているのだ。
rows.en: She and I were, in fact, trading partners.

ghs.en: Her and I will, in fact, be trading.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that she and Taichi actually have an established trading relationship. The English uses an object pronoun as subject and changes the standing arrangement into a future transaction.

highlights.text: Her and I will, in fact, be trading.

rows.jp: 手を叩く。

ghs.en: I clap my hands.

rows.jp: 視線がこちらを向いた。

ghs.en: The gaze turned my way.

rows.jp: 一切れのピザを眼前に。
rows.en: I held a slice of pizza in front of her.

ghs.en: I hold a slice of pizza in front of her eyes.

rows.jp: 興味を示した。

ghs.en: She showed interest.

rows.jp: つかもうとする。

ghs.en: She tries to take it.

rows.jp: ちょっと離れるとつかもうとするのをやめる。
rows.en: When I drew it back a little, her hand stopped.

ghs.en: I take it a bit farther, and she ceases trying to take it.

rows.jp: 半径３０センチの距離。これが彼女の聖域だ。
rows.en: Thirty centimeters. That radius was her inviolate territory.

ghs.en: That is her sanctuary: a radius of 30 centimeters of distance.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese states a thirty-centimeter radius. The English redundantly attaches 'of distance' and produces an unnatural measure phrase.

highlights.text: a radius of 30 centimeters of distance

rows.jp: 思案し、少女は弁当箱を掲げる。俺に。
rows.en: After a moment’s thought, the girl held her lunch box up to me.

ghs.en: She ponders, then the girl sets out the lunchbox. Towards me.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says the girl holds up or presents her lunchbox to Taichi. 'Sets out' instead suggests placing or arranging it, while the detached direction fragment obscures the action.

highlights.text: sets out the lunchbox. Towards me.

rows.jp: 「ＯＫー」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Okieeeh!"

rows.jp: 卵焼きをひとつもらった。
rows.en: I took one piece of rolled omelet.

ghs.en: I took one fried egg,
ghs.assessment: 卵焼き here is tamagoyaki, a rolled omelet, not a fried egg.

rows.jp: で、かわりにピザを進呈する。
rows.en: I gave her the pizza in return.

ghs.en: and, in exchange, offer the pizza.
Girl: "..."

rows.jp: はむはむと食べはじめる。

ghs.en: Munch, munch she begins to eat down.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese simply says she begins munching. 'Eat down' is not idiomatic for beginning to eat the offered food.

rows.jp: 「とまあこのように」

ghs.en: Taichi: "And, well, sort of like this."
Kiri: "...what was that now?"

rows.jp: 「物々交換が基本なんだ。あのこ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Bartering is foundation. For her."
ghs.assessment: The English omits the article in 'is the foundation/basis' and strands the qualifier 'for her' as a fragment.

rows.jp: 「あとは自分の世界だけでいい。だから半径３０センチ外の出来事には、関心が薄いんだ」
rows.en: “The rest of the time, her own world is enough. She has little interest in anything beyond that thirty-centimeter radius.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "After that, she's fine with just her own world. Therefore, all that happens outside the radius of 30 centimeters she shows minimal interest in."

rows.jp: 「サヴァン症候群的な面もある。単純計算が異常にできる。あと数百年先のカレンダーの日にちと曜日をぴたりと即答する」
rows.en: “She has savant-syndrome traits too. She can do simple calculations at impossible speed, and instantly name the weekday for any date hundreds of years from now.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "She has similar symptoms to a Savant syndrome as well, an abnormal ability to make simple calculations. Ask her about what day of the week it will be on a date several centuries ahead, receive an immediate exact reply."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says she also has savant-syndrome-like aspects. The English treats the syndrome as a countable symptom and uses the ungrammatical collocation 'symptoms to.'

highlights.text: similar symptoms to a Savant syndrome

rows.jp: 「数字の海を眺めてるんじゃないかな」
rows.en: “Maybe she spends her time gazing out over a sea of numbers.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Maybe she's just lost in the contemplation of an ocean of numbers."

rows.jp: 「……幸せなんですか、それであの人は？」

ghs.en: Kiri: "...but can that girl be happy with that?"

rows.jp: 「当然」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Naturally."

rows.jp: 「幸せの形が、人と違うだけさ」
rows.en: “Her happiness simply takes a different shape from other people’s.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "The shape happiness takes is different between people, that's all."

rows.jp: 「……そんなのいやです」

ghs.en: Kiri: "...that is not right."
ghs.assessment: Kiri says she does not want or cannot bear that kind of existence. The English recasts her aversion as a moral judgment that it is incorrect.

rows.jp: 「悪意はないのかもしれないけれど、わたしはそんなのはいやです」
rows.en: “Maybe no one means any harm, but I still can’t stand it.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "There might not be malice or anything, but, that is not right to me."
ghs.assessment: Kiri says that even if there is no malice, she still hates or rejects such a state. The English turns her emotional refusal into a claim about correctness.

highlights.text: that is not right to me

rows.jp: 「だって……人がいるのに……一人一人が絶海の孤島みたいで……閉じてて……」
rows.en: “Because... there are people all around, but every one of them is shut off like an island in the middle of the ocean...”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Because... when people exist... to still exist one by one as if solitary islands on distant seas... closed off..."
ghs.assessment: Kiri says that even with people present, each person is closed off like an isolated island. The English repeats 'exist' in an ungoverned infinitive and does not form a complete clause.

highlights.text: when people exist... to still exist one by one

rows.jp: 「いやなんです……」

ghs.en: Kiri: "That is just not right..."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese repeats Kiri's personal 'I don't like it.' The English again substitutes an impersonal judgment that it is wrong.

ghs.en: Taichi: "......"

rows.jp: まるで霧は、
rows.en: It was as though Kiri were crying out—

rows.jp: かまってください―――

ghs.en: "Care about me, please---"

rows.jp: そう叫んでいるように見えた。

ghs.en: had been shouting that.

rows.jp: 「それが君の傷か」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Is that your wound then?"
Kiri: "...eh?'
ghs.assessment: The dialogue opens with a double quotation mark but closes with a single quotation mark.

rows.jp: 新川が呻く。

ghs.en: Shinkawa groans.

rows.jp: 「お、お兄チャマが起きそう」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Oh, looks like Onii-chama's waking up."
ghs.assessment: The deliberately childish distortion of 'older brother' is left as an unexplained Japanese kinship form rather than represented in English.

rows.jp: 「豊のこと好きなの？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Do you really like-like Yutaka?"

rows.jp: 「それは…………って、な、何言ってるんですかっ」

ghs.en: Kiri: "Well, I...... wait, wh-, what are you talking about?!"

rows.jp: 赤くなった。

ghs.en: She went red.

rows.jp: 「あっ、だからっ、違いますっ」
rows.en: “No! I told you, that isn’t it!”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Ah! Seriously! Not like that!"

rows.jp: 「わかりやすい」

ghs.en: Taichi: "So easy to understand."

rows.jp: 「違いますってばっ」

ghs.en: Kiri: "It is not like that, I'm telling you!"

rows.jp: 「いいなあ豊」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Nice, eh, Yutaka."
ghs.assessment: いいなあ豊 means that Yutaka is lucky or fortunate. The English instead reads as Taichi telling Yutaka that something is nice.

ghs.en: Kiri: "...ehhh?"

rows.jp: 豊が無言で起きた。

ghs.en: Yutaka woke up without a word.

rows.jp: 目をこする。

ghs.en: He rubs his eyes.

rows.jp: 「……やべ、また落ちた、俺…………あれ、俺のピザは？」
rows.en: “...Damn, I passed out again............ Hey, where’s my pizza?”

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "...no way, I fell asleep again, I did...... eh, where's my pizza?"

rows.jp: 「食べちゃった」

ghs.en: Taichi: "All eaten."

rows.jp: 「なん、だと……？」

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "What... the...?"

rows.jp: 唖然とする。

ghs.en: Mute amazement.

rows.jp: 「だって起きるとは思ってなかったから」
rows.en: “I didn’t think you were going to wake up.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But I didn't think you were going to wake up, so..."

rows.jp: 豊は低く呻いた。

ghs.en: Yutaka gave a low moan,

rows.jp: が、それ以上文句を言う様子はなかった。
rows.en: But he showed no sign of complaining further.

ghs.en: but outside of that, there didn't seem to be any further complaints.
Shinkawa: "..."

rows.jp: かわりに別のことに興味を引かれたようだ。
rows.en: Something else seemed to have caught his attention.

ghs.en: Instead, he seems to have been caught into a different interest.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says something else caught his interest. 'Caught into an interest' is not an English construction.

rows.jp: 俺を見る。

ghs.en: He looks at me,

rows.jp: 赤面している霧を見る。

ghs.en: he looks at Kiri's red face,

rows.jp: 腕を組んで考える。
rows.en: He folded his arms and considered.

ghs.en: and he thinks with folded arms.

rows.jp: 豊は再度霧を見あげた。
rows.en: Yutaka looked up at Kiri once more.

ghs.en: Then Yutaka looked one more time up at Kiri.

rows.jp: 「ＯＫ、事情はわかった……で、縁談はまとまったのか？」
rows.en: “Okay, I see what happened... So, is the match settled?”

ghs.en: Shinkawa: "O.K., I get the situation... marriage proposal's all proper and submitted then?"
ghs.assessment: 縁談はまとまった asks whether the marriage arrangement has been settled. The English invents submission and does not idiomatically express an arrangement being finalized.

highlights.text: marriage proposal's all proper and submitted then?

rows.jp: 「明日式だ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ceremony's tomorrow."

rows.jp: 「しませんっ！！」
rows.en: “There is not going to be a wedding!”

ghs.en: Kiri: "It is not!!!"
ghs.assessment: Kiri says that she will not do it, in context rejecting the proposed marriage. The English substitutes an impersonal statement that something is not.

rows.jp: そんなことがあった。

ghs.en: And that was one of the things that happened.
